title: plugin-security: sys_user_permission_set.granted_by is a plain lookup, so a granter row that no longer resolves is filed as a dangling business reference and keeps cloud's hourly integrity WARN red
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect, reach measured. Cloud's production control plane raises the hourly `[integrity] stored references that resolve to nothing (#4551)` WARN on every run. One of its findings is `sys_user_permission_set#ups_d85cfc63b091b7b1.granted_by` → `sys_user#manual:db-cutover-superadmin`, 1 of 13 rows in the 2026-09-15 reading (objectstack-ai/cloud#2274, comment 5673661010).

Found by the objectstack-ai/cloud#2274 dev (os-dev-report, objectstack-ai/cloud#2274 comment 6053481678, which carries the measurement and the draft below). Filed by the `repo:cloud` seat (`repo:cloud#1`, R45, session `session_011jobP72PwN3whNm55GetXQ`), because the fix lands in this repo. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The defect (read at `56bf27af`, cloud's pin)

- `packages/objectql/src/integrity/dangling-reference-audit.ts` (about :470) routes a finding by `readonly === true` alone. A `readonly` reference that resolves to nothing goes to `provenance`, and the WARN condition (about :735) does not include `provenance`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts:84`: `granted_by` is `Field.lookup('sys_user', { required: false, … })`, not `readonly`. So a granter that is gone, or a sentinel, raises the alarm as a broken business reference.
- This repo already treats the column as provenance: `auto-org-admin-grant.ts:785` says "[#4586] The provenance the row already had a column for". It also quotes ADR-0118 D1 (:786–788): "an id or null, never a sentinel".
- The family shares the shape:
  - `sys_user_position.granted_by` (`sys-user-position.object.ts:106`);
  - plugin-sharing `sys_record_share.granted_by` (`sys-record-share.object.ts:230`).
  Each needs its own measurement.

## Fix (the dev's draft; measure first)

- Add `readonly: true` to `granted_by`, and to each family member after measuring it.
- **Measure the writer first.**
  - `delegated-admin-gate.ts` (:645, :781, :820) stamps `granted_by = ctx.userId` only when the value is null ("never overwrite an explicit value").
  - With `readonly`, an explicit caller value that the gate leaves alone is stripped by `stripReadonlyFields`, so the row lands NULL.
  - Either the gate always stamps the writer on non-system inserts, or #14088's hook-write record must be shown to keep the gate's stamp.
  - System-context writers keep their value: `invitation-placement.ts:204`, `auto-org-admin-grant.ts:790` and `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:1138`.
- **The dev's open question, for this lane to settle:**
  - A: `readonly`, and the gate always stamps the writer on non-system inserts.
  - B: `readonly` only, relying on #14088.
  - C: no `readonly`, with an audit-side exemption.
  - The dev recommends A, so that "granted_by = writer" becomes enforced. C is a consumer-side carve-out, which contract-first rules out. B leaves a silent NULL path.
- **Test:** a row whose `granted_by` names a deleted user lands in `provenance`. As a positive control, a business lookup still lands in `dangling`.

**Not in scope:** the production row holds a sentinel string. Nulling it is a production write, and it needs cloud's maintainer.

## Done when

- A `granted_by` that resolves to nothing is filed under `provenance`, and the WARN no longer fires on it.
- A non-system caller cannot set an arbitrary granter.

## Reach and timing

- Cloud consumes this repo by pin and stays on `56bf27af` until v18 (#22050, ruling B), so the fix reaches cloud's alarm with v18.
- The rest of objectstack-ai/cloud#2274 lands in cloud's PR #2678: the usage rows become provenance, and `sys_import_job` is created. After that, this column is the WARN's last finding.

## Reader

Triage routes it. By its package it lands in the `plugin-security` lane.

## Dedupe

A semantic search for `granted_by readonly provenance dangling reference audit sys_user_permission_set` finds 27 issues, all of them adjacent and none this defect (the closest are #21861, #21669 and #21455). The dev's dedupe words are: `granted_by readonly provenance`, `dangling-reference audit granted_by`, `db-cutover-superadmin` and `delegated-admin-gate granted_by explicit value`.
